modules.name: seed
owns: Demo dataset: one manager (role MANAGER) and one employee (role EMPLOYEE, managerId -> manager) with bcrypt password hashes minted via bcrypt.hashSync(plaintext, 10) — the same call AuthService verifies with
Leave types (annual, sick) and their ACTIVE leave policies (annualEntitlementDays, accrualPeriodMonths, carryForwardDays, minNoticeDays, maxRequestDays)
One leave_balances row per employee per leave type for the CURRENT accrual period, derived via shared/date periodContaining anchored on hireDate (never a hand-written date)
Two or three leave_requests in different states (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED) with requestedDays computed via shared/types requestedDays
Balance-counter consistency: SUBMITTED request days appear in pending_days, APPROVED days in used_days (derived from the seeded requests, never hardcoded independently)

Idempotency: detect an already-seeded row by composite key (employee, leave_type, start_date for requests; email/employee_number for employees; code for leave types; leave_type_code for policies; employee+leave_type+period_start for balances) and skip rather than duplicate or delete
knex seed entry (001_demo_data.js) that registers ts-node and delegates to the seed service

modules.name: dev-runner
owns: Concurrent process orchestration: spawn the API (npm run start) and the web dev server (npm run dev in web/) together
Forward both children's stdout/stderr to the parent terminal with a per-process prefix
Forward exit codes: when either child exits, terminate the sibling and exit with the child's code
Signal handling so Ctrl-C tears down both children

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Seed module + knex wiring + npm run seed
recommended_phases.rationale: Foundational: the demo dataset is the dependency every later step documents. Deliver the seed service (idempotent, bcrypt hashes, current-period balances, balance-counter consistency), the knex seed entry, the knexfile.js seeds config for the development environment, and the root `npm run seed` script.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Dev runner + npm run dev
recommended_phases.rationale: Independent of the seed; delivers scripts/dev.js and the root `npm run dev` script so the documented command exists and works.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — web test script fix
recommended_phases.rationale: One-line change to web/package.json (`vitest` -> `vitest run`) so the test command exits instead of entering watch mode.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — README documentation
recommended_phases.rationale: Last, because it documents the exact commands (migrate, seed, start API, start web, npm run dev) and demo credentials that the prior phases make real.

app_notes: This feature adds no API surface and no role-gated access — it delivers development-only data (a knex seed), a process orchestration script, npm scripts, and documentation. Therefore authContract and errorResponseContract are intentionally empty. The seed module is a new top-level module under seeds/ (not src/modules/) because it is development data, never part of the runtime application; it depends only on shared-types (enums + requestedDays) and shared-date (periodContaining) so balance periods and requested-day counts are derived from the same canonical helpers the services use, never hand-written. Balance counters are derived from the seeded requests (SUBMITTED -> pending_days, APPROVED -> used_days) so they cannot drift. Idempotency keys: employees by email/employee_number, leave_types by code, policies by leave_type_code, balances by (employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start), requests by (employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date). The seed must never run as part of migrate — it is wired only into the development environment's seeds config in knexfile.js.

open_questions.question: How should the demo account password be supplied to the seed and documented?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether the README documents a fixed literal password or an env-var-driven one, and whether the seed hardcodes a credential string (no-hardcoded-secrets constraint).
candidate_options: Hardcode a clearly-demo password (e.g. 'demo-password') in the seed and README — acceptable because it is a dev-only demo credential, not a real secret
Read DEMO_PASSWORD env var with a documented default, mirroring scripts/smoke.js SMOKE_PASSWORD pattern

auth_contract: This feature exposes no API endpoints and no role-gated access (seed data, dev runner, npm scripts, docs). No auth contract applies.
error_response_contract: This feature exposes no API endpoints. No error/response contract applies.
